overview: This guide walks you through comparing AutoVision and Stable Diffusion 3.1 for edge image generation, and shows how to build a no‑code AI workflow using PromptFlow. It covers setting up API access, creating a workflow, and tips for optimizing image quality.
key_takeaways: AutoVision delivers high‑resolution, vibrant images with crisp details, ideal for commercial graphics.
Stable Diffusion 3.1 offers a more artistic, rustic style and can be run locally or via the Hugging Face Inference API.
PromptFlow lets you combine multiple AI models into autonomous workflows without writing code.
You can drag‑and‑drop API connectors in PromptFlow to mix AutoVision and Stable Diffusion outputs.
Testing workflows live in PromptFlow helps quickly iterate on prompt and model selection.
prerequisites: API keys for AutoVision, Stable Diffusion 3.1 (Hugging Face), and PromptFlow.
Basic understanding of REST APIs and JSON payloads.

step_by_step.title: Step 1: Set Up API Credentials
step_by_step.description: Create accounts on AutoVision, Hugging Face, and PromptFlow. Store the API keys in environment variables for secure access. On a Unix shell, export them as:
step_by_step.code_example:
```bash
export AUTOVISION_API_KEY=your_autovision_key
export HF_API_KEY=your_huggingface_key
export PROMPTFLOW_TOKEN=your_promptflow_token
```

step_by_step.title: Step 2: Test Image Generation APIs
step_by_step.description: Verify that each image model is reachable by sending a simple POST request. Use curl or a small Python script to generate a test image.
step_by_step.code_example:
```bash
# AutoVision
curl -X POST https://api.autovision.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUTOVISION_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "A futuristic city skyline", "size": "1024x1024"}' > autovision.png

# Stable Diffusion 3.1 via Hugging Face
curl -X POST https://api-inference.huggingface.co/models/stabilityai/stable-diffusion-3.1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"inputs": "A fantasy landscape"}' > sd3.1.png
```

step_by_step.title: Step 3: Build a PromptFlow Workflow
step_by_step.description: Log into PromptFlow’s web UI, create a new workflow named "Edge Image Generator", and drag connectors for AutoVision and Stable Diffusion. Configure each step to accept a prompt, pass the result to the next step, and store the image URLs in a final output node. After building, click the "Run" button to execute the workflow and preview images side‑by‑side.

pro_tips: Use PromptFlow’s built‑in parameter tuning to adjust temperature and guidance scale for each model to balance creativity and fidelity.
Cache image outputs in a CDN or cloud storage to reduce API call costs during repeated comparisons.
Leverage PromptFlow’s branching logic to route prompts to the model that historically produces better results for a given category (e.g., landscapes vs portraits).
common_pitfalls: Pitfall 1: Forgetting to set the correct image size in the API payload; this can lead to truncated or low‑resolution images.
Pitfall 2: Exceeding API rate limits by running multiple parallel workflows; always monitor quota usage in the dashboard.

faq.question: Can I run Stable Diffusion 3.1 locally instead of using the Hugging Face API?
faq.answer: Yes, download the model weights from Hugging Face and run them on a GPU‑enabled machine using the official Stable Diffusion repo.

faq.question: How do I compare image quality metrics between AutoVision and Stable Diffusion?
faq.answer: Use perceptual similarity metrics like LPIPS or SSIM on a set of test prompts, and store the scores in PromptFlow’s output node for analysis.

faq.question: What if my prompt includes copyrighted text or imagery?
faq.answer: Both AutoVision and Stable Diffusion enforce content policies; ensure your prompts comply with their terms of service to avoid rejection.

faq.question: Can I integrate other models, such as DALL‑E 3, into the same PromptFlow workflow?
faq.answer: Yes, add a new API connector for DALL‑E 3 and configure the workflow to route prompts to it based on user selection.
